ideas.author: Percy Greg
ideas.line: A vehicle designed to travel through outer space rather than air or water.
ideas.name: Astronaut (Ship)
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: Carriers and expedition firms buy ships, and many yards could build them once shown how, so established vehicle builders collect.
verdict.prize_why: A working vessel for travel between worlds would found a transport industry of its own.

ideas.author: W.S. Lach-Szyrma
ideas.line: A ship built to sail through space beyond the atmosphere.
ideas.name: Ether Ship
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: Carriers and expedition firms buy ships, and many yards could build them once shown how, so established vehicle builders collect.
verdict.prize_why: A working vessel for travel between worlds would found a transport industry of its own.

ideas.arrival: built in the 1930s, about 50 years after it was imagined
ideas.author: Albert Robida
ideas.line: A screen that carries live images and sound from far away into the home.
ideas.name: Telephonoscope
ideas.profit: a monopoly-like profit, kept by platforms

verdict.money_why: Households buy sets and pay for channels, and since sets are easy to copy, the firms that own the factories, the stations and the networks collect.
verdict.prize_why: Seeing distant events live at home changed how most people spend their evenings and learn the news.

ideas.arrival: built in the 2000s, about 120 years after it was imagined
ideas.author: Edward Bellamy
ideas.line: Rooms wired to carry live concerts from distant halls so listeners can hear them whenever they like.
ideas.name: Telephonic Music Room
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by platforms

verdict.money_why: Listeners pay a regular fee, and since the wiring is easy to copy, the firms that already own the music and the lines into homes collect.
verdict.prize_why: Hearing any concert at home whenever you like is how most music now reaches people, and it is worth an industry.

ideas.arrival: built in the 2020s, about 140 years after it was imagined
ideas.author: Jules Verne
ideas.line: Projecting huge commercial messages onto the clouds so entire cities can see them.
ideas.name: Atmospheric Advertising
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by licence holders

verdict.money_why: Advertisers pay, and anyone with a strong projector can light up the sky, so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: Messages on the clouds are one more place to show advertisements, and they depend on the weather.

ideas.arrival: built in the 1980s, about 100 years after it was imagined
ideas.author: Jules Verne
ideas.line: Reporters speak the day's events directly to subscribers as they happen rather than printing them.
ideas.name: Live News
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by licence holders

verdict.money_why: Subscribers pay, sending speech is easy to copy, and the firms that already gather the news collect.
verdict.prize_why: News spoken to subscribers as it happens is worth an industry of its own.

ideas.arrival: built in the 2010s, about 130 years after it was imagined
ideas.author: Jules Verne
ideas.line: A device for two-way conversation where each party both hears and sees the other.
ideas.name: Phonotelephote
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by platforms

verdict.money_why: Ordinary people buy it; the screens and cameras are easy to copy, so the firms that own the networks collect.
verdict.prize_why: Seeing the person you talk to changes how families keep in touch and how firms meet.

ideas.arrival: built in the 1990s, about 110 years after it was imagined
ideas.author: Jules Verne
ideas.line: Storing spoken news so listeners can replay it whenever they choose.
ideas.name: Recorded News

verdict.money_why: Readers pay; the machine is easy to copy, so the news firms that already gather the reports collect.
verdict.prize_why: Getting the news at the moment and place you choose is a convenience over waiting for the paper.

ideas.arrival: built in the 2000s, about 120 years after it was imagined
ideas.author: Mary E. Bradley Lane
ideas.line: Making edible nutrients through chemistry and fermentation instead of growing crops.
ideas.name: Chemical Production of Food

verdict.money_why: Households buy it as ordinary groceries, and since the method can be copied, the food makers who already own plants, brands and shop space collect.
verdict.prize_why: Food made without fields would free the feeding of people from land and weather, which touches nearly everyone.

ideas.arrival: built in the 1930s, about 50 years after it was imagined
ideas.author: Mark Twain
ideas.line: A wire barrier charged with current strong enough to stop anyone from crossing.
ideas.name: Electrified Fence

verdict.money_why: Farms and guarded sites buy it, and wire with a current through it is simple for anyone to supply.
verdict.prize_why: A charged fence keeps animals in and people out, which is useful but narrow.

ideas.work: A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court

ideas.author: Percy Greg
ideas.judged: AI models judge it not physically possible
ideas.line: A material that repels gravity strongly enough to carry a vessel between planets.
ideas.name: Apergy (Apergion)
ideas.profit: not judged (not a technology, not something sold, not physically possible, or unclear)

verdict.money_why: Carriers, builders and launch firms would pay, and since the trick could be copied once shown, the firms that already build vehicles and craft would collect.
verdict.prize_why: Cancelling weight at will would cut the cost of lifting, carrying and launching, which changes transport and building more than it changes how most people live.

ideas.author: Edward Page Mitchell
ideas.judged: AI models judge it not physically possible
ideas.line: An old clock whose reversed motion carries people into the past.
ideas.name: Dutch Clock (Time Machine)
ideas.profit: not judged (not a technology, not something sold, not physically possible, or unclear)

verdict.money_why: I assume a state would keep for itself a machine that can alter history, so a government pays and its established contractors build it, since others could copy it once shown.
verdict.prize_why: Reaching the past would be worth an industry in study, salvage and statecraft, though few people would need it day to day.

verdict.prize_why: Reaching the past would be worth an industry in study, salvage and statecraft, though few people would need it day to day.

ideas.author: Jules Verne
ideas.judged: AI models' likeliest decade: 2100 or later
ideas.line: Shoving the whole planet with an enormous force so its spin axis stands upright and seasons vanish.
ideas.name: Straightening the Earth's Poles
ideas.profit: not judged (not a technology, not something sold, not physically possible, or unclear)

verdict.money_why: Only a government could pay for a work on the whole planet, and the firms that already build its great works collect.
verdict.prize_why: Ending the seasons is a public work whose gain the description does not name, and the story's promise leaves out the harm to coasts and climates.

ideas.work: The Purchase of the North Pole (Topsy Turvy)

ideas.arrival: built in the 1950s, about 70 years after it was imagined
ideas.author: Edward Bellamy
ideas.line: A card carried instead of cash that lets people pay for goods against an account.
ideas.name: Credit Card
ideas.profit: a monopoly-like profit, kept by platforms

verdict.money_why: Shops and banks pay fees on each sale, and since the card or chip itself is easy to copy, the banks and payment networks that already hold people's accounts collect.
verdict.prize_why: Paying without cash is worth an industry of its own, and the card drawn on an account is its plainest form.

ideas.arrival: built in the 1950s, about 70 years after it was imagined
ideas.author: Edward Bellamy
ideas.line: A single large covered building holding many stores together.
ideas.name: Mall (Great City Bazaar)
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: Shopkeepers pay for space, and since the building is easy to copy, the owners of well-placed land collect.
verdict.prize_why: Many stores under one roof changed how shopping is done and is an industry of its own.
